Featuring bar down, batted, and brilliant blasts from Owen Power, Tim Stützle, Mason McTavish, Lucas Raymond, Evan Bouchard, Kirill Marchenko and more!

Each pack contains 1 Next-Gen Class highlight, 2 Stadiums & Skylines highlights, 1 Base 2023-24 highlight, plus 1 mystery highlight that could be from Next-Gen Class (75%), Guardians of the Net (12.9%), Opening Ice 2023-24 (10%), Cause for a Celly: ‘90s (2%), or The Greatest Achievements sets (<1%).

release.name: Next-Gen Class Debut LE Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Thursday February 29, 2024 at 1PM ET / 10AM PT

 

Price: $29 USD

# Packs Available: 3,000

 

Purchase Limit: Ten (10) pack limit per person for the first 24 hours; limit increased to fifty (50) pack limit per person afterwards. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 5

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) highlight from Next-Gen Class (Limited #/500)
  • Two (2) highlights from Stadiums & Skylines (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight from Base 2023-24 (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 75% Next-Gen Class (Limited #/500)
    • 12.9% Guardians of the Net (Limited #/500)
    • 10% Opening Ice 2023-24 (Rare #/250)
    • 2% Cause for a Celly: ‘90s (Epic #/100)
    • 0.1% The Greatest Achievements (Legendary #/10)

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay where available; where not available, payments will be processed via Stripe.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. A Marketplace Fee may be incurred upon resale. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included:

  • Full Highlights List
  • Next-Gen Class, Series 1 - Preview
  • Stadiums & Skylines, Series 1 - Preview
  • Base 2023-24, Series 1 - Preview
  • Guardians of the Net, Series 1 - Preview
  • Opening Ice: 2023-24, Series 1 - Preview
  • Cause for a Celly: ‘90s, Series 1 - Preview
  • The Greatest Achievements, Series 1 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 1 highlights will only be distributed during Series 1, which ends ~September 2024. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

summary.name: Next-Gen Class
summary.description: Elevate your collection with the Next-Gen Class set, spotlighting young players already making waves as contributors to their teams. Although no longer rookies, they look to represent part of the future. These highlights showcase the skills and impact of these up-and-coming stars as they strive to shape their franchise's future.

summary.name: Stadiums & Skylines
summary.description: Introducing "Stadiums & Skylines," a set that celebrates the thrilling past and present moments from a diverse array of NHL outdoor games. This unique collection showcases iconic stadiums and breathtaking skylines as the backdrop to unforgettable hockey events. Immerse yourself in the excitement of these outdoor spectacles with "Stadiums & Skylines," where the magic of hockey meets the awe-inspiring settings that make these games truly extraordinary.

summary.name: Guardians of the Net

"Guardians of the Net" is a celebration of the artistry and resilience displayed by these contemporary net guardians, showcasing their remarkable ability to defy the odds and keep their teams in the game.

summary.name: Cause for a Celly: '90s
summary.description:
The Cause For A Celly: '90s collection immortalizes unforgettable NHL playoff highlights from the '90s that helped define the sport, featuring many of the game's greatest players and iconic moments that have left an indelible mark on hockey history.

Relive the exhilarating moments, featuring both legendary players and game or series-changing plays. From stunning overtime goals to game-saving glove saves, Cause For A Celly: '90s captures the drama, passion, and intensity of the playoffs like never before.

This exclusive set delves into the annals of NHL history, bringing to life the brilliance of great players and the unforgettable moments that have shaped the postseason.

summary.name: Alex Ovechkin
summary.description:
On Dec. 23, 2022, Alex Ovechkin surpassed “Mr. Hockey,” Gordie Howe, for second place on the NHL’s all-time goals list behind “The Great One,” Wayne Gretzky. “The Great 8” has had a remarkable career having won the Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy on nine occasions – the most any NHL player has finished as single-season goals leader. Ovechkin tops a list of only three players to lead the League in goals more than five times, the others being Bobby Hull (7x) and Phil Esposito (6x). For his first goal of the game (801), the play begins with Ovechkin feeding the puck to teammate Ryan Strome on the far side in the neutral zone. As Strome gains the blue line, Ovechkin trails the play getting the drop pass where he walks it in and zips it five-hole past the netminder. In the final play, Ovechkin gains the blue line with the puck where he has a clear shot at the empty net. Instead, he pulls up and passes it over to longtime teammate Evgeny Kuznetsov. Kuznetsov dishes it back to Ovechkin where he spins alongside the boards and throws it into the empty net in front of an elated home crowd, with his teammates then flooding the ice in celebration.

summary.name: Mario Lemieux
summary.description:
In a defining moment of the 1991 Stanley Cup Final against the Minnesota North Stars, Mario Lemieux delivered a goal that would become iconic. This extraordinary play paved the way for the Pittsburgh Penguins to secure their first-ever Stanley Cup victory. With the Penguins holding a 2-1 lead late in the second period, Lemieux takes control of the puck deep in his own zone and swiftly sets off, building momentum as he moves up the ice. Crossing the blueline, Lemieux showcases his unmatched skill by gracefully maneuvering past two Minnesota defenders. With a quick shift of the puck onto his backhand, he expertly places it beyond the reach of goaltender Jon Casey. The goal not only showcased Lemieux's brilliance but also propelled the Penguins closer to their championship triumph. Throughout the playoffs, Lemieux displayed incredible prowess, leading to him being awarded the prestigious Conn Smythe Trophy. His exceptional performance included registering an impressive 44 points in just 23 games, ranking as the second-highest number of playoff points ever recorded in a single season in NHL history.
